pr_title: Fix cannot update remote after disabling `use_global_coordinates` in `RemoteTransform2D`
pr_body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.
PRs can target `3.x` if the same change was done in `master`, or is not relevant there.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.

To speed up the contribution process and avoid CI errors, please set up pre-commit hooks locally:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/code_style_guidelines.html
-->

Due to the optimization in `CanvasItem`, `global_transform` is only updated when `get_global_transform()` is called, and then notify `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`. That is, in the case where `global_transform` is not obtained, the notification `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` will not be sent.

So we use `NOTIFICATION_LOCAL_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` in this case. Use in combination to prevent certain optimizations.

Fix https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83297#issuecomment-1762815741.

Same change for `RemoteTransform3D`, to prevent the same optimization from being used in Node3D in the future.
pr_comments:
Provide a scene for testing.
[node_2d.tscn.txt](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/12905724/node_2d.tscn.txt)


> Due to the optimization in `CanvasItem`, `global_transform` is only updated when `get_global_transform()` is called, and then notify `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`. That is, in the case where `global_transform` is not obtained, the notification `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` will not be sent.

That's not really true as both Node2D and Control do call `CanvasItem::_notify_transform` from their methods when their local transform is being changed.

So AFAICT for RemoteTransform2D the `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` is being sent just fine when its `transform` changes. Meaning regardless of the value of `use_global_coordinates` the updating already works.

Given all this, this PR still makes sense because when `use_global_coordinates == false` then RemoteTransform2D still propagates its local transform on any change of its global transform. And that's not needed, in such case the propagation is needed only when the local transform changes (if global transform changes because some parent transform has changed then it's irrelevant).



https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp#L890-L892

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp#L181

This flag doesn't seem to change in `Node2d`/`Control`. The optimization still works. Maybe `get_global_transform()` is called somewhere else.
I wrongly assumed that `_set_global_invalid(true)` is called only from `CanvasItem::_notify_transform`. :man_facepalming:

But because it's called on `NOTIFICATION_PARENTED`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp#L371-L376
and because `NOTIFICATION_PARENTED` is received before a node is added to the tree, then it results in `is_inside_tree()` check to fail:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/main/canvas_item.cpp#L896-L907
Hence after such CanvasItem is added to the SceneTree it's marked as having invalid global but it's not added to the `SceneTree::xform_change_list` which would result in propagating `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/main/scene_tree.cpp#L179-L190

Seems like potentially a bigger issue? :thinking:

---

 Regarding specifically the changes in this PR the 2D part looks good to me anyway. I haven't dived into 3D notifications.
> Regarding specifically the changes in this PR the 2D part looks good to me anyway. I haven't dived into 3D notifications.

There is currently no relevant optimization in 3D. If it is not needed, I can reset that commit.

> I wrongly assumed that _set_global_invalid(true) is called only from CanvasItem::_notify_transform.

`_set_global_invalid(false)` is only called in `CanvasItem::get_global_transform()`, so calling this method (or `get_global_*()`) is a necessary condition for notify `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED` next time.

Edit: 
Also worth noting is the name of this flag: `global_invalid`, `false` means `global_transform` is **valid**. 
That is, if `get_global_*()` is not called, `global_transform` is **invalid** and `global_invalid` is `true`.



> There is currently no relevant optimization in 3D. 

Indeed, so what I've said in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/83323#issuecomment-1762896443 is true for the RemoteTransform3D (but not for the RemoteTransform2D because of the discussed optimization). Meaning only 2D was bugged.

>If it is not needed, I can reset that commit.

No, the changes are good. :+1: Quoting myself (just replace RemoteTransform2D with RemoteTransform3D):

> Given all this, this PR still makes sense because when `use_global_coordinates == false` then RemoteTransform2D still propagates its local transform on any change of its global transform. And that's not needed, in such case the propagation is needed only when the local transform changes (if global transform changes because some parent transform has changed then it's irrelevant).

Thanks!

issue_context.title: RemoteTransform2D projects wrong position
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.2.beta

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

I assume the main use-case of `RemoteTransform2D` is to have another node match the transform of the `RemoteTransform2D`'s parent node. When `RemoteTransform2D` has `use_global_coordinates` set to `false`, however, the position sent to the controlled node will be the `RemoteTransform2D`'s local position, which makes sense, I guess, but that will always be `(0,0)`. This could be the expected behavior, but I can't imagine when it'd ever be useful, so please correct me if I'm wrong. 

### Steps to reproduce

1. Make a sprite.
2. Make a second sprite with a `RemoteTransform2D` child and move it anywhere on screen.
3. Select the first sprite as the `RemoteTransform2D`'s target.
4. Set `use_global_coordinates` to false.

### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
There seems to be something strange here.

When `use_global_coordinates` is `true`, it will notify `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`; when `use_global_coordinates` is `false`, it will not.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/2d/remote_transform_2d.cpp#L68-L72

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a574c0296b38d5f786f249b12e6251e562c528cc/scene/2d/remote_transform_2d.cpp#L88-L92

Here, `get_global_transform()` seems to be a necessary condition for notify `NOTIFICATION_TRANSFORM_CHANGED`.

> I assume the main use-case of `RemoteTransform2D` is to have another node match the transform of the `RemoteTransform2D`'s parent node.

@markdibarry This seems to be a wrong assumption. According to the docs (and to the source code) RemoteTransform2D is supposed to propagate its own transform to the target node, not the transform of RemoteTransform2D's parent.

Given that's indeed intended by design, I see no bug in here.

So in the MRP you'd rather want the sprite to be a child of RemoteTransform2D, and you'd move the RemoteTransform2D (instead of its child sprite) so its `transform` would be propagated to the other sprite.

---

Changing RemoteTransform2D to propagate the parent's transform instead would be a compatibility breaking change. But I guess what could be done is adding a bool like `propagate_parent_transform` (false by default for compat) which would make the RemoteTransform2D behave as you've assumed it to behave. But something like this is a material for a proposal, not for a bugfix.

@kleonc Yeah, I guess that's the part I was confused about. I threw this in as an issue because, as far as I can glean, it works exactly as it says, I just can't imagine a scenario where the intended design would ever be useful without completely negating the need for the node in the first place. I honestly only use this node to do quick mock ups for things, and would never use it for an actual system, so it's not a high priority for me, but I was playing around with a `SubViewport` and needed to switch to local `position`, and was confused at how literally it behaved. It reminds me of that Daffy Duck bit where he uses a disintegration pistol and the pistol disintegrates. Like, yep, that makes total sense, but not helpful.

I totally agree: it *does* do what it says it does, but if it's intended to be used with `RemoteTransform2D` as the parent of the object to follow, I cannot find one example out there of it being used this way even as far back as Godot 2... and I imagine would make things very problematic to do so, especially if the child is a `CharacterBody2D` or anything with logic in it. The `global_transform` works perfectly for how every example I have found uses it, but it just kinda happens to work, if it's not intended to work like that at all. I think you're right about it needing a compatibility property, but it's just funny how useless it is in its current state despite doing exactly as it says.

review_comments: Probably makes sense to also add such guards to other setters (`set_use_position` etc.).
